blocks.text: OAuth/OIDC vulnerabilities arise when authorization responses, tokens or linked identities are not bound to the correct client, issuer, user session and redirect destination. OAuth authorization and OIDC authentication have different token and validation requirements.

items: Issuer mix-up and ID-token audience validation

blocks.text: Provision two test users, two clients and a controlled authorization server. Capture a working authorization-code flow and mutate one parameter at a time. Query strings below are fragments for the authorization endpoint; token bodies are form-encoded replacements. Substitute registered lab identifiers and freshly issued test values. Omission of state is not itself proof of a flaw when another correct CSRF defense binds the flow.

Verify the logged-in subject, issuer, client and granted scope after each operation. Reusing an authorization code should fail. A verifier mismatch must fail for a PKCE-bound code. Account-link tests require explicit confirmation and a recent session according to application policy. Use JWT-Vulnerabilities for claim-level token fixtures and Session-Management for lifecycle sequences.
See `oauth-oidc-payloads.txt` for parameter variants and two-session sequences. Placeholder codes and tokens must be replaced only with locally issued lab values.

files.name: oauth-oidc-payloads.txt

sections.label: State binding: absent, empty, incorrect and other-browser values; evaluate the complete CSRF defense
Nonce validation applies to an OIDC ID token and its initiating flow
Redirect URI validation: compare with the exact registered callback
PKCE variants: use codes actually issued with an S256 challenge in the baseline
Scope elevation requests: consent and client policy must constrain grants
Issuer mix-up callback fragments; only a valid signed token from the expected issuer may authenticate
Account linking: use two owned identities with matching display email but different stable subjects/issuers
Refresh lifecycle: reuse a consumed refresh token under a rotation-enforcing policy
Missing PKCE challenge on a client configured to require PKCE
Token exchange without a required verifier
Authorization-code replay: repeat the same locally issued code, client and verifier
Account-link callback with another browser's state/code; use two owned test users
Userinfo substitutions: OIDC uses sub as the stable subject identifier

files.content:
# OAuth / OIDC Testing Payloads
# Query and form fragments, not complete authorization requests. Use registered test clients and a local IdP.

# State binding: absent, empty, incorrect and other-browser values; evaluate the complete CSRF defense
state=oauth-unmatched-state
state=&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a
state=LAB_OTHER_BROWSER_STATE
state=oauth-state-first&state=oauth-state-second

# Nonce validation applies to an OIDC ID token and its initiating flow
nonce=oidc-unmatched-nonce
nonce=&scope=openid%20profile
nonce=LAB_OTHER_FLOW_NONCE

# Redirect URI validation: compare with the exact registered callback
redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test.untrusted.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback
redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%40untrusted.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback
redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback%2Fextra
redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Funtrusted.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback
redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback

# PKCE variants: use codes actually issued with an S256 challenge in the baseline
code_challenge_method=plain&code_challenge=oauth_lab_plain_challenge_012345678901234567890123456789
code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge=not-a-valid-s256-challenge
code_challenge_method=unsupported&code_challenge=oauth-lab-unsupported
code_verifier=oauth_lab_wrong_verifier_012345678901234567890123456789
code_verifier=

# Authorization-code exchange bodies
grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&code=LAB_CODE_FOR_CLIENT_B&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback&code_verifier=LAB_MATCHING_VERIFIER
grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&code=LAB_ALREADY_USED_CODE&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback&code_verifier=LAB_ORIGINAL_VERIFIER
grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&code=LAB_FRESH_CODE&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fother-client.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback&code_verifier=LAB_MATCHING_VERIFIER

response_type=token&response_mode=query
response_type=code%20id_token&response_mode=form_post
response_type=none&response_mode=query

# Scope elevation requests: consent and client policy must constrain grants
scope=openid%20profile%20oauth-lab-admin
scope=openid%20offline_access
prompt=none&max_age=0

# Issuer mix-up callback fragments; only a valid signed token from the expected issuer may authenticate
iss=https%3A%2F%2Fother-idp.example.test
iss=https%3A%2F%2Fidp.example.test.untrusted.test

# Account linking: use two owned identities with matching display email but different stable subjects/issuers
{"provider":"oidc-lab","subject":"oauth-lab-subject-b","email":"oauth-link-user@example.test","email_verified":false}
{"provider":"oidc-lab-other-issuer","subject":"oauth-lab-subject-a","email":"oauth-link-user@example.test","email_verified":true}

# Refresh lifecycle: reuse a consumed refresh token under a rotation-enforcing policy
grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&refresh_token=LAB_ROTATED_REFRESH_TOKEN
grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=oauth-lab-client-b&refresh_token=LAB_CLIENT_A_REFRESH_TOKEN

# Missing PKCE challenge on a client configured to require PKCE
/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback&scope=openid&state=oauth-no-pkce-state&nonce=oauth-no-pkce-nonce

# Token exchange without a required verifier
grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=oauth-lab-client-a&code=LAB_S256_BOUND_CODE&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.example.test%2Foidc%2Fcallback

# Authorization-code replay: repeat the same locally issued code, client and verifier
curl -sS 'https://idp.example.test/token' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=authorization_code' --data-urlencode 'client_id=oauth-lab-client-a' --data-urlencode 'code=LAB_ONE_USE_CODE' --data-urlencode 'redirect_uri=https://client.example.test/oidc/callback' --data-urlencode 'code_verifier=LAB_ORIGINAL_PKCE_VERIFIER'

# Account-link callback with another browser's state/code; use two owned test users
/oidc/link/callback?code=LAB_USER_B_CODE&state=LAB_USER_A_STATE&iss=https%3A%2F%2Fidp.example.test

# Userinfo substitutions: OIDC uses sub as the stable subject identifier
{"sub":"oauth-lab-subject-b","email":"oauth-link-user@example.test","email_verified":false}
{"sub":"oauth-lab-subject-b","email":"oauth-link-user@example.test","email_verified":true}
